abilities.description: Rebuilds and tunes solar crawlers, mirrors and pressure tools with salvaged parts.
abilities.name: Crawler Fieldcraft

abilities.description: Interprets Sunspire Array control logs and satellite uplink protocols.
abilities.name: Uplink Reading

characters.arc: Tamsin learns that engineering alone cannot save the Greenhold. She comes to trust Orrin's knowledge and the Dustwalkers' guidance, and she chooses to share the vault's codes and seeds rather than use them for personal vindication.
characters.description: Seventeen-year-old apprentice engineer of Greenhold Westreach, raised in the mirror-tending crews of the Sunspire Array. Small and wiry, she has sun-freckled skin, short copper-dyed braids, and a belt of pressure-wrench tools she rarely takes off. Her mother was an Array Warden who vanished on a failed repair climb, leaving Tamsin a battered logbook of satellite uplink procedures.
characters.external_conflict: The Westreach Council forbids unauthorized trips into the Wastes, and the Dustwalkers demand tolls she cannot pay.
characters.flaw: Reckless self-reliance; she improvises first and consults others later, and she hides fear behind bravado.
characters.goal: Reach the Deepseed Vault and recover the old codes needed to take back control of the rogue satellite.
characters.internal_conflict: She fears she is repeating her mother's fatal overreach, yet cannot bring herself to wait for permission or help.
characters.motivation: To save Westreach from Helios Wake and prove her mother's belief that the satellite could be reclaimed.
characters.name: Tamsin Vale

abilities.description: Breeds and revives crops that survive scorching light and thin soils.
abilities.name: Heat-Tolerant Cultivation

abilities.description: Remembers the oral landmarks and passphrases that lead to the Deepseed Vault.
abilities.name: Seedkeeper Lore

characters.arc: Orrin moves from guarded solitude to open teaching. He trusts Tamsin with the full route and publicly claims the Seedkeeper principle in front of the Council.
characters.description: A sixty-year-old botanist who left Westreach decades ago and lives among the living walls on the arcology's edge. Tall and stooped, with weathered brown hands, a lichen-green shawl and a cough from old dust exposure. He is one of the last Seedkeepers who remembers the oral route to the Deepseed Vault.
characters.external_conflict: The Council wants vault stock under arcology control, and he is wary of ever trusting its officials again.
characters.flaw: Secretive and distrustful of the young and of authority; he withholds crucial knowledge until forced to share it.
characters.goal: Guide Tamsin to the Deepseed Vault and ensure its seed stock is distributed to all Greenholds.
characters.internal_conflict: He swore to guard the vault's location, yet protecting it now means letting the Greenholds starve.
characters.motivation: To honor the Seedkeeper oath that seeds belong to everyone, and to atone for a past silence that cost lives.
characters.name: Orrin Ashgrove

abilities.description: Plans power and food allocation to stretch scarce supplies.
abilities.name: Rationing Strategy

abilities.description: Persuades and pressures the Council and citizens to follow his decisions.
abilities.name: Political Command

characters.arc: Faced with the solar storm and the heroes' proof, Marek accepts that hoarding endangers everyone. He opens the arcology's stores and agrees to share the seed stock with all Greenholds.
characters.description: The fifty-year-old chair of the Westreach Council. Broad-shouldered and neat, he wears a pale-green ration-ledger pin and speaks in measured tones. He led Westreach through two lean winters and now believes any risk to the arcology's stores is a betrayal of its people.
characters.external_conflict: He clashes with the Array Wardens over spare parts and with the Seedkeepers over ownership of the seeds.
characters.flaw: Controlling and fearful; he mistakes hoarding for safety.
characters.goal: Keep any vault seed stock and satellite codes under Council authority and stop unsanctioned expeditions.
characters.internal_conflict: He knows the seed-sharing custom is sacred, yet fears that sharing will leave Westreach with nothing.
characters.motivation: To keep Westreach alive through rationing, order and control of every resource.
characters.name: Councilor Marek Holloway

abilities.description: Reads dust storms, glass drifts and ruins to find safe crossing routes.
abilities.name: Waste Navigation

abilities.description: Barters for and repairs sealed filters and crawler parts.
abilities.name: Filter Trading

characters.arc: Kesra shifts from transactional guide to committed ally. She spends her own filters and standing to help the heroes finish the journey, and she sets up a fair trade pact.
characters.description: A forty-year-old Dustwalker guide and trader based at Rustmarket Halt. Lean and sun-darkened, she wears a sail-cloth cloak, patched filter mask and a necklace of tiny seed pods. She has crossed the Glasswind Wastes more times than she can count and keeps a map in her head.
characters.external_conflict: The Dustwalkers resent arcology outsiders, and Kesra must justify her choice to guide Westreach folk.
characters.flaw: Mercenary and suspicious; she hides generosity behind hard bargaining.
characters.goal: Guide the heroes across the Wastes in exchange for a lasting trade agreement with Westreach.
characters.internal_conflict: She wants to help the heroes for free, but fears undermining her clan's hard-won bargaining position.
characters.motivation: To secure her clan's survival and win fair dealing from arcology folk.
characters.name: Kesra Dunmoor

abilities.description: Repairs mirrors, photovoltaic fields and the Sunspire control hall.
abilities.name: Array Maintenance

abilities.description: Teaches young engineers with patience and clear explanation.
abilities.name: Mentoring

characters.arc: Juno finds the courage to defy the Council openly. She prepares the Array for the codes and stands with Tamsin in the final confrontation.
characters.description: A twenty-eight-year-old senior Array Warden and Tamsin's mentor after her mother's disappearance. Compact and soft-spoken, with grease-stained gloves and a habit of humming while she works. She was a friend of Tamsin's mother and holds her unfinished repair notes.
characters.external_conflict: The Council withholds spare parts the Wardens need to keep the uplink alive.
characters.flaw: Overprotective and conflict-averse; she avoids confronting the Council even when she disagrees.
characters.goal: Keep the Sunspire uplink running and prepare it to accept the vault's codes.
characters.internal_conflict: She wants to support Tamsin's mission openly, but risks losing her post and the Wardens' access to the Array.
characters.motivation: To finish the work her friend started and protect Tamsin from the same fate.
characters.name: Juno Pell

relationships.description: Tamsin Vale and Orrin Ashgrove are uneasy partners on the crossing; her impulsiveness grates against his secrecy, but each holds knowledge the other needs.
Councilor Marek Holloway forbids Tamsin Vale's expedition and treats her as a reckless threat to Westreach's stores, creating pressure on her journey.
Councilor Marek Holloway and Orrin Ashgrove clash over who controls the vault's seeds; Marek once exiled Orrin's Seedkeeper circle from official gardens.
Juno Pell mentors Tamsin Vale, shields her from Council scrutiny and holds the notes of Tamsin's missing mother.
Kesra Dunmoor guides Tamsin Vale across the Wastes for payment, and the bargain slowly becomes real trust as Tamsin repairs her crawler.
Kesra Dunmoor has traded seeds with Orrin Ashgrove for years and trusts his word, which helps persuade her to take the mission.
Juno Pell resents Councilor Marek Holloway's hoarding of spare parts, though she avoids open defiance until the storm nears.
